text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has told Albania to close down pyramid schemes.
- Police evacuated more than 100 cafes and bars in the centre of the capital Tirana when an anonymous caller said a bomb had been planted there but it turned out to be a hoax.
- Police have recovered a priceless 13th century embroidery on canvas, central to Albanian heritage, known as the Gllavenica epitaph, and several other relics.

- The government has failed to listen to criticisms of Albania's May general polls by an Organisation of the Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) group, although it agreed to allow an OSCE delegation to monitor local polls on October 20. - The Albanian government has set up a commission to negotiate the return of Albanian gold looted by Hitler's Nazis at the end of World War Two and held in London under the custody of an Anglo-French-U.S. commission.

- With winter approaching, the government has decided not to tax liquid gas in a drive to get citizens to use gas instead of electricity for heating, because of the poor state of the electricity distribution grid.

- Albanians thronged to medical centres on Monday to be vaccinated at the start of an immunisation campaign against a polio virus which has claimed 12 lives so far. Some 100,000 people were registered in Tirana alone.

- The key opposition Socialist Party has mobilized 12,000 people to detect potential irregularities in voting lists for the forthcoming polls, fearing the ruling Democratic Party could add fake names to the lists to increase its own votes.
- The government has decided that officials dealing with the sale of tax stamps will retain a three percent profit.
- President Sali Berisha has visited ten major towns around the country to campaign for his party's candidates for the posts of mayor and commune head.
